title: Pumpkin cinnamon rolls
equipment: Stand mixer with dough hook, or a large bowl

items: ½ cup whole milk, warmed to 105–110°F
1 cup canned pumpkin purée (not pumpkin pie filling)
¼ cup unsalted butter, melted and slightly cooled
4 cups all-purpose flour, plus up to ¼ cup more for kneading
1 Tbsp softened butter, for the bowl and pan
⅓ cup unsalted butter, very soft

steps: Stir the yeast and 1 tsp of the brown sugar into the warm milk. It should feel warm, not hot (105–110°F). Wait 5–10 min, until foamy. If it doesn't foam, the yeast is dead; start over with fresh yeast.

Add the rest of the brown sugar, the pumpkin, egg, melted butter, salt, pumpkin pie spice and 3½ cups of the flour. Mix on low with the dough hook (or a wooden spoon) until a shaggy dough forms, then add the last ½ cup flour.
Knead on medium-low 6–8 min (8–10 min by hand), until smooth and springy. It stays a little sticky. Add more flour 1 Tbsp at a time only if it sticks to everything.
Put the dough in a greased bowl, cover and let it rise in a warm spot 1–1½ hr, until doubled.

Grease a 9×13-inch pan. Roll the dough on a lightly floured counter into a 16×12-inch rectangle. Spread the soft butter over it, leaving a ½-inch bare strip along one long edge. Mix the brown sugar and cinnamon and sprinkle it evenly over the butter.

Roll up tightly from the long side opposite the bare strip and pinch the seam closed. Cut into 12 rolls about 1⅓ inches wide. Set them cut side up in the pan, cover and let rise 45 min, until puffy and touching. Heat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the middle during the last 20 min.
Bake 22–26 min, until golden brown and the center roll reads 190°F. Cover loosely with foil after 15 min if the tops brown too fast.
Beat the cream cheese, butter, powdered sugar and maple syrup until smooth. Let the rolls cool 10 min, then spread the icing over them while still warm.
tips: Overnight option: after shaping, cover and refrigerate up to 16 hr. Let them sit at room temperature 45–60 min before baking.
Cut the log with unflavored dental floss. Slide it under, cross the ends and pull; it won't squash the rolls.
If the pumpkin looks watery, blot it with paper towels first, or the dough will need a lot more flour.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days, covered, because of the cream cheese icing. Freeze un-iced baked rolls up to 2 months. Rewarm in the microwave 15–20 sec, or covered in a 300°F oven 10 min.
